blocks.text: After breakfast, a city tour of Quito, rich in history and culture: panoramic views, historic churches and beautifully decorated rooftops, with insights into the colonial art and architecture of the capital. Founded in the 16th century on the ruins of an Inca city, at about 2,850 m, Quito survived several earthquakes and keeps one of the best-preserved historic centres in Latin America, with ornate interiors showcasing the Quito School of Art, a fusion of Spanish, Italian, Moorish, Flemish and Indigenous influences; it was among the very first places inscribed on UNESCO’s World Heritage List.

**Ciudad Mitad del Mundo** is a visitor and shopping complex north of central Quito.

Its monument commemorates the **1736 geodetic expedition**, which set out to establish the position of the Equator.

The monument, about **30 metres** high, was erected between 1979 and 1982. A line marking the Equator runs from its centre.

Later GPS measurements placed the actual line about **240 metres north** of the monument.

blocks.text:
Your second stop is the **Intiñán Museum**, with interactive exhibits on how ancient peoples located the Equator and experiments such as balancing an egg on a nail.

The museum also introduces the cultures of ancient South American peoples. Its grounds display totems from different cultures and traditional Ecuadorian homes. You can see a house containing objects that belonged to an Indigenous family who lived here generations ago.

After the tour, return to Quito. Overnight at Hotel Finlandia 4★. Breakfast is included.
